description.fun: Bagon dreams of flying, so it leaps from high cliffs every day in hopeless attempts and burns with envy at the sight of bird Pokémon. It vents its frustration by headbutting rocks, which has made its head as hard as steel. That longing to fly is thought to be written in its genes, and it's been seen flapping its arms in its sleep.
description.guide: A Dragon-type Pokémon resembling a small dragon with a domed head, living alone in rocky terrain among the cliffs. It evolves into Shelgon at level 30.
description.tagline: A stubborn little dragon that leaps off cliffs dreaming of flight

description.fun: Shelgon is wrapped in a shell made of the same substance as bone, so heavy it can barely move, and it hides away in caves while its cells rebuild its body. It neither eats nor drinks the whole time, living on stored energy and its long-held dream of flight. When it's finally ready to evolve, the shell peels off all at once.
description.guide: A Dragon-type Pokémon resembling a pupa inside a hard shell of bone-like plates, which hides in caves while it waits to evolve. It evolves from Bagon at level 30 and into Salamence at level 50.
description.tagline: A dragon in its cocoon, rebuilding itself to fly

description.fun: Salamence's lifelong wish to fly finally made its cells mutate and sprout wings, and now it can't stop: it flies around joyfully breathing fire and only lands when it's worn out and needs to sleep. If it gets angry, it loses all control and wrecks everything around it until it tires itself out. It even flutters its wings in its sleep. Its name blends salamander and menace.
description.guide: A Dragon- and Flying-type Pokémon based on a European dragon, which sprouted wings through sheer longing to fly. It evolves from Shelgon at level 50 and is the final form of Bagon. It can Mega Evolve with the Salamencite.
description.tagline: A dragon whose dream of flight came true at last

description.fun: Mega Salamence's wings fuse into a single huge crescent, hard yet flexible enough to slice through anything in its path, and it flies like a fighter jet. The stress of having its beloved wings reshaped makes it rampage, sometimes turning on its own Trainer, and it is feared as 'the blood-soaked crescent'. The Paradox Pokémon Roaring Moon is said to be an ancient relative of it.
